name: What’s the difference between a bump-out and a full home addition?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a bump-out and a full home addition?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a bump-out and a full home addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bump-out is a smaller extension that enlarges part of a room, such as a kitchen, bathroom, or primary suite. It usually adds modest square footage and is often used to improve layout, circulation, or storage. A full home addition is larger and creates a complete new functional area, such as an extra bedroom, bathroom, family room, or second-story suite. The difference matters because budget, permitting, and structural complexity are not the same. A bump-out may be less expensive and faster if it avoids major structural changes, but it may not solve a space shortage on its own. A full addition delivers more usable space but typically requires more engineering, plan review, and construction time. Homeowners should choose the option that solves the actual problem, not just the one that seems cheaper. If the goal is to improve a cramped kitchen, a bump-out may be enough. If the goal is to add a new bedroom for a growing family, a full addition is usually the better investment.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bump-out is a small extension of an existing room, usually designed to add limited square footage without creating a new full room. A full home addition adds a complete new space such as a bedroom, suite, or family room.
